title: Cohort-driven Model Evolution Orchestrator
creator: Alex Chen
body:
Problem: Teams need a safe, automated way to run controlled exposures of new model versions that respect user cohorts, preserve statistical validity across staggered ramps, and enable rapid auto-rollback on negative signals. Current A/B/canary tooling focuses on flat exposure percentages and lacks cohort-level controls, sequential testing primitives, and integrated shadow validation for behavioral regressions.

Goal: Design and deliver an A/B testing framework that orchestrates cohort-aware experiments for model versions (canaries, staggered ramps, multi-variant), enforces exposure budgets, runs sequential statistical checks with alpha spending or Bayesian credible-intervals, supports shadow traffic and offline backfills, and wires auto-rollback triggers into the rollout controller and the Console. The feature should be usable by product/ML teams via Redwood Console and the Redwood API.

Scope: MVP covers cohort definition (by property or sampled buckets), exposure schedules (time-based ramps and percent-by-cohort), a statistical test library (frequentist sequential tests + Bayesian estimation), auto-rollback policy hooks, and observability panels (cohort-level metrics, test trajectories, drift alerts). Integrations include rollout API, serving runtime labels, and Optimize suggestions for recommended ramp sizes and test thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Console: UI to define cohorts and attach them to an experiment with independent exposure schedules
API: /rollouts endpoint accepts cohort config, exposure schedule, and statistical policy in a single manifest
Runtime: serving runtime receives per-request cohort tag and honors routing to specified model variant or shadow path
Stats: experiment runs sequential checks and emits pass/fail decisions per cohort and global aggregation
Auto-rollback: rollout controller aborts and reverts traffic on defined safety failures and writes audit events
Observability: per-cohort time-series and test results available in Console with links to raw evaluation traces
Simulation: offline simulation harness that validates planned ramp + test policy against historical traffic in a staging dataset
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): finalize cohort schema, exposure budget model, and statistical policies with Research and Data Science
Phase 1 (API + Runtime): extend rollout manifest -> ENG implements cohort tags in runtime, add routing rules
Phase 2 (Console + UX): PM+Design build experiment builder with schedule editor and safety policy form
Phase 3 (Stats + Safety): Research implements sequential testing primitives and auto-rollback rule engine
Phase 4 (Pilot): run 3 internal pilots (search, autocomplete, reranking), iterate on thresholds
Phase 5 (GA): documentation, SDK examples, Optimize recommendations for common templates
statistical_plan: Support two testing modes: Frequentist sequential testing with alpha spending (O'Brien-Fleming) and Bayesian A/B estimation (beta-binomial for CTR-like metrics)
Default thresholds: two-sided alpha 0.05 with alpha-spend schedule; Bayes default: 95% credible interval excluding control value
Sequential checks evaluated on rolling windows and after minimum sample size per cohort to avoid early false positives
Multiple comparisons correction for multi-cohort / multi-metric experiments using Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control
Safety signals: prioritized guardrail metrics (error-rate, severe-toxicity proxy, latency P95). Any metric breach marked as high-severity triggers immediate rollback policy evaluation
Statistical results exported as JSON events (p-values, effect sizes, credible intervals) for Console and Alerting
observability_and_metrics: Per-cohort dashboards with primary and guardrail metrics and view into test statistic trajectories
Alerting rules: sustained negative delta (effect size < threshold for N minutes) or guardrail breach -> Slack + PagerDuty when severity==high
Audit log entries for each rollout decision: who initiated, which policy fired, revert PR/commit links
Trace links from Console to raw request examples and token-level diffs for content regressions
Cost telemetry: token and GPU utilization per cohort to detect cost regressions during experiments
integrations: Serving runtime tagging: attach cohort and variant to KV-cache keys to preserve cache efficiency
Optimize: recommend initial ramp sizes and min sample requirements based on workload latency and cost profiles
Console: experiment builder, timeline view, and one-click rollback action that triggers runtime route switch
Data warehouse exports: event-level experiment data for retrospective analysis
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased tail latency when mirroring/shadow traffic -> Mitigation: cap shadow sampling rate and run shadow on same hardware class where possible
Risk: false positives from frequent peeking -> Mitigation: sequential testing with pre-registered alpha spend and min N enforcement
Risk: cohort imbalance causing noisy estimates -> Mitigation: stratified randomization and diagnostic imbalance reports before checks start
Risk: rollback flapping during intermittent upstream incidents -> Mitigation: require multi-signal confirmation (stat + guardrail) and cooldown period before automated rollback repeats
comments: 2026-01-19 Alex Chen: Initial problem write-up and proposed goals. Shared with Research and ENG for feedback.
2026-01-28 Priya Kapoor: Synced with Research. They recommend supporting Bayesian first for small-traffic cohorts; Research will prototype.
2026-02-05 Jordan Blake (Engineering): Raised runtime concerns about KV cache fragmentation when routing by cohort — ENG-3021 created to prototype cache-preserving keys.
2026-02-22 Design review: UX proposals prefer template-based experiment creation to reduce misconfiguration. Designer: Maya Rivera.
2026-03-03 Research note: alpha-spend schedule draft attached to PR; recommends min N=500 per cohort for CTR-like metrics; considering sequential permutation tests for non-parametric metrics.
2026-03-10 Priya Kapoor: Planning to kick off Phase 1 after ENG-3021 spike completes. Next: align API contract and add schema validation to rollout manifest. Assigned to ENG-5188 for API changes.
